calibration: expected calibration error over 10 confidence bins

criteria.adopt: log loss favours the negative binomial, calibration is preserved, balanced accuracy is not degraded, and home_active recall does not favour the hurdle-Poisson
criteria.balanced_accuracy: question 4, from the primary estimand: not degraded if negligible or favouring the negative binomial, degraded if favouring the hurdle-Poisson, uncertain otherwise
criteria.calibration: question 2: preserved if calibration error does not favour the hurdle-Poisson in the primary estimand and favours the negative binomial against the declared rates; lost if it favours the hurdle-Poisson, or is negligible or favours the declared rates against them; uncertain otherwise
criteria.complexity: extra complexity is never accepted because one metric improves: adoption needs the log-loss gain and every guard
criteria.log_loss: question 3, from the primary estimand: improves, no change, worsens or uncertain
criteria.overall: adopt if adopted in both settings, reject if rejected in both, and otherwise not adopted, with each setting's decision reported
criteria.recall: question 1, from the primary estimand's home_active recall: recovers if it favours the negative binomial, no change if negligible, loses more if it favours the hurdle-Poisson, uncertain otherwise
criteria.reject: log loss is negligible or favours the hurdle-Poisson: the extra parameter is not accepted, whatever else improves
criteria.trade-off: log loss favours the negative binomial, but calibration is lost, or balanced accuracy or home_active recall favours the hurdle-Poisson
criteria.verdicts: favours model: mean >= delta and lower bound > 0; favours reference: mean <= -delta and upper bound < 0; negligible: the whole interval within (-delta, delta); uncertain: anything else

dispersion.classes: poisson (alpha 0); moderate (below extreme); extreme, low data; extreme, flat; extreme, supported
dispersion.flat: the observed table's log-likelihood at alpha exceeds that at alpha / 2 by less than 1 nat: weakly identified
dispersion.question: extreme estimates indicate insufficient data if more than half of them are low data; otherwise they are not a data shortage
dispersion.recorded: each fold's alpha, size, mu and active mean per channel and state, with its active training windows

estimands.question: the negative binomial against the hurdle-Poisson, current windows
the negative binomial against the declared rates, current windows: is the calibration improvement preserved
the hurdle-Poisson against the declared rates, current windows, as in the Phase 3.3 follow-up

fitting.hurdle: pi = (Z + k pi0) / (W + k); m = (S + k m0) / (P + k); mu solves mu / (1 - exp(-mu)) = m
fitting.hurdle_nb: the same pi and m; alpha maximises the profile likelihood of the active-count table plus k pseudo-windows distributed as the zero-truncated Poisson with mean m, over {0} and [1e-4, max_dispersion]; mu solves the zero-truncated negative binomial's mean for m

households.use: each household is held out once; its fold's training households fit every channel model

identical: prior, transition, channels, windows and inference; the models differ only in each channel's observation model
inference: online filter: I0 and R read no window after the scored one

declared.emissions: default_emissions of the household registry, pooled per channel
declared.fitted: nothing: every parameter is the declared default
declared.prediction: most probable state of the posterior; no abstention
declared.prior: stationary distribution of the default ontology, one step before the first declared window
declared.transition: default StateOntology, time-homogeneous, one step per window
declared.windows: the set's current window, plus its lagged windows with recent history

hurdle.emissions: per channel and state: P(silent) = pi, and a zero-truncated Poisson with rate mu for an active window's count
hurdle.fitted: pi and mu per fold, per channel and state, on the fold's training households' labelled windows only, shrunk toward the declared model by the pseudo-windows
hurdle.model: restricted generative filter with fitted hurdle channels
hurdle.prediction: most probable state of the posterior; no abstention
hurdle.prior: stationary distribution of the default ontology, one step before the first declared window
hurdle.transition: default StateOntology, time-homogeneous, one step per window
hurdle.windows: the set's current window, plus its lagged windows with recent history

hurdle_nb.emissions: per channel and state: P(silent) = pi, and a zero-truncated negative binomial with mean mu and dispersion alpha for an active window's count
hurdle_nb.fitted: pi and the active mean as for the hurdle; alpha maximises the profile likelihood of the training households' active-count table plus the pseudo-windows, Poisson-shaped at the same mean; per fold, channel and state, on the fold's training households only
hurdle_nb.model: restricted generative filter with fitted hurdle negative-binomial channels
hurdle_nb.prediction: most probable state of the posterior; no abstention
hurdle_nb.prior: stationary distribution of the default ontology, one step before the first declared window
hurdle_nb.transition: default StateOntology, time-homogeneous, one step per window
hurdle_nb.windows: the set's current window, plus its lagged windows with recent history

motivation: the posterior predictive checks found the zero-truncated Poisson active count systematically under-dispersed, with a variance growing with the square of the mean; their routing named within-state temporal dependence as the next family, which a count distribution cannot address, and this experiment measures what the over-dispersed count alone does
name: phase3-hurdle-negative-binomial

per_state_recall.rare_rule: share of labelled time below 0.05 in either fold's training households

questions.1: does the negative binomial recover some of the home_active recall the hurdle-Poisson lost
questions.2: does it preserve the calibration improvement
questions.4: does it avoid degrading balanced accuracy
questions.settings: each question is answered in each setting from its primary estimand, N0 or NR, and for calibration also D0 or DR

quiet_runs.comparison: paired household difference, lower is better
quiet_runs.setting: the recursion only: a fully silent window has the same likelihood under both hurdle families, so with current windows their slopes coincide
quiet_runs.statistic: Phase 3.3's accumulation slope: within the predicted state, the least-squares slope per hour of confidence minus correctness on the position in a run of consecutive fully silent windows, over labelled windows at positions 1 to 36

settings.R: the filter's recursion fed every window of the recording from the stationary distribution; every model receives the same windows

tuning: none: every setting is declared here, before scoring
